messages:
Maria H: Quick flag — p95 for the v2.3 canary spiked ~18% on long-seq runs in the evening smoke. Seeing it across eu-west-1 nodes. Should we rollback or collect a couple of quick profiles before deciding?
Cheng Li: Which workload exactly? long-seq sampling or streaming?
Maria H: long-seq sampling (2k tokens, temp 0.7). Baseline p95 ~420ms, canary ~495ms on identical hardware.
Sam K: Can you paste the run command you used so I can reproduce locally?
Maria H: Sure — run used: ```./scripts/perf-run.sh --model redwood-v2-3 --seq 2000 --warm 50 --samples 150 --mode sampling```
perf-bot: summary from latest run -> p50: 120ms, p95: 495ms, p99: 720ms (eu-west-1 canary cluster, 2026-03-17T21:12Z)
deploy-bot: Canary health check: node-pressure=high on 3/8 hosts, fallback activated on route /v1/generate (partial)
Rafael P: I can grab KV cache hit profiles and a couple of perf samples in ~15m. If it's kernel-level, rollback might be faster.
Cheng Li: Could be a batching interaction with the new scheduler change. If someone can run a small bisect: run with scheduler=v1/v2 and compare p95. I can script that.
Sam K: +1 for collecting a small set of targeted profiles before full rollback. We should avoid flapping if it's config. Also want flamegraphs.
Micah (oncall): Operational stance: if client-facing latency SLOs are breached for >10% of requests for >30m we should rollback. Current impact window ~18m and ~12% of requests affected. I'm leaning wait 20m for profiles then decide.
Maria H: OK Rafael + Cheng — can you run the bisect/profiles now and drop results here? If you hit obvious kernel/alloc regression, call rollback.
Rafael P: Starting profiler now. Will post a link to traces + flamegraphs when done.
Cheng Li: I'll run the scheduler v1/v2 quick comparison and post numbers.
perf-bot: scheduled jobs: profile-2283456123 (expected finish ~2283456560)
Sam K: placing +rollback vote if profiles implicate runtime change. Otherwise hold.
Maria H: noted. tagging @oncall for visibility.
Micah (oncall): thanks. If Rafael posts evidence pointing at runtime change I'll call the rollback. Keep me updated. :thumbsup:
Rafael P: uploaded flamegraphs -> https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/2283456123/flame.html. Early look shows increased syscalls in kernel memcopy path on large batches.
Cheng Li: my quick comparison: scheduler=v1 p95=428ms, scheduler=v2 p95=494ms. Delta matches. Looks like scheduler change is the likely culprit.
Sam K: that's pretty decisive. I'm switching to rollback vote.
Maria H: Agreed. Micah, do you want to initiate rollback now?
Micah (oncall): initiating rollback to previous runtime snapshot v2.2 on eu-west-1 canary. ETA ~8m. Notifying infra.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by Micah (oncall) for cluster eu-west-1, target snapshot v2.2. Job id rb-2283456701
Maria H: thanks all — ping here when rollback completes and we'll re-run the same perf-run to confirm p95 recovery.
perf-bot: rollback job rb-2283456701 completed at 2283456888, health checks green
Rafael P: re-ran perf-run.sh after rollback: p95=425ms, p99=710ms — back to baseline.
Maria H: great, closing this thread. We'll open a followup to revert scheduler change after a quieter test window. :white_check_mark:
